ns2:course.label: Advanced Bibliographic Metadata
ns2:course.description: Seminar on theoretical and applied approaches to cataloging, including the creation and management of complex descriptive and subject metadata. Topics include current developments in conceptual models for bibliographic materials; information processing and mapping; socio-cultural and critical warrant; and ethical foundations of information organization. Students will engage critically with principles and practices in the application of bibliographic standards in a variety of contexts. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit. Prerequisite: IS 507 or consent of instructor.
